messages:
Claire: Heads-up: PMs want a clear cost-guardrail for the residency feature before we flip beta to customers. Need decisions on charge-preview, burst limits, and rollback semantics. Short sync?

Arjun: Agree. Primary ask: Console must show estimated token-cost delta per region and per-model if tenant pins to region. Also need an API preview endpoint.

Marta: From product: customers will ask for a dry-run so they can see cost + perf before opting in. Proposal: 48h dry-run with logs and a cost-estimate email at end.

Sanjay: Ops perspective: add a soft cap and hard cap for per-tenant QPS. Soft cap throttles with polite 429 + header X-Cap-Mode:soft, hard cap rejects with 403 and audit log.

Lena: UX note: Show both incremental monthly cost and sample p50/p99 changes. Also surface warnings when enabling could cause eviction from cheaper shared pools.

Arjun: Implementation idea: add charge-preview API: POST /v1/tenants/:id/preview-policy with policy blob -> returns {estimated_monthly_delta_usd, changes:[{model,region,per_token_delta}], warnings:[string]}. We'll need offline simulator for accuracy.

Claire: That API works. Add in-console modal that requires user to type the tenant name to confirm (for enterprises).

Marta: Acceptance criteria for beta:
- Preview API accuracy within 15% of observed delta in dry-run
- Dry-run logs retained 72h and downloadable
- Soft cap behavior validated at scale (no >5% error increase)

Sanjay: Operational runbook: when soft cap triggers >1% of requests for 10m, auto-create incident and move tenant to throttled pool. Recovery path: backoff window or manual override.

Lena: On billing disputes: keep an immutable snapshot of the preview results and the dry-run logs. Also add a hologram banner in the console: "Preview is an estimate; final charges may differ".

Arjun: Risk: bursty tenants enabling residency could exhaust reserved regional capacity and spike latency for pinned tenants. Mitigation: admission control + per-tenant burst credits.

Claire: Define burst credits: each tenant starts with N credits based on historical 95th percentile QPS * 10 minutes. Credits consumed on excess QPS and replenish daily. If credits exhausted, soft-cap behavior ramps to hard cap.

Marta: That seems fair. For pricing we should have an explicit surcharge table for regional pins vs baseline. E.g., +X% for region-residency in expensive regions.

Sanjay: Also need a rollback strategy: policy toggle timeline -> dry-run -> canary (1% tenants) -> regional canary across 1 AZ -> ramp. Include automatic rollback heuristics when p99 latency increases by >20% or error rate +5% absolute.

infra-bot: Canary deployment queued: policy-enablement/canary at commit f1d2d2 queued to infra-runner. Check /ci/canary-logs.

Arjun: Telemetry: add per-tenant token/cost delta + 'pin-violation' metric when we route outside preferred region due to capacity constraints. Alert on >0.1% pin-violation.

Lena: Console element: "Enable residency" flow should show
- Preview numbers
- Burst credit explanation
- Estimated surcharge
- Dry-run toggle (checkbox) with dates

Claire: Launch checklist draft:
1) Preview API and console modal implemented
2) Dry-run infra + logs + download
3) Admission control + burst credit system in staging
4) Ops runbook + auto-rollback heuristics
5) Two reference customers validated in dry-run
6) Billing surcharge table approved by finance

Marta: Time estimates: Preview API (2 sprints), dry-run infra (3 sprints), burst credits + admission (3 sprints), runbook + rollback (1 sprint). Can parallelize.

Sanjay: Test plan: run synthetic load with mixed pinned/unpinned tenants, simulate region loss, measure tail latencies and pin-violation rate.

Arjun: Small technical note: preview simulator needs accurate cost model: tokenization differences, quantized model throughput, egress differences per region. I'll pair with Finance.

Lena: Customer messaging: add an "Impact summary" PDF generated from preview that PMs can send to customers. Auto-attach dry-run logs if requested.

Claire: Ok owners: Arjun (preview API + simulator), Sanjay (admission control + runbook), Lena (console + messaging), Marta (acceptance + customer outreach). Sync Fri 10am PT.

Marta: One last risk: legal/data residency contracts may insist on hard-residency even if region fails. We need legal to confirm acceptable fallback semantics.

Claire: Good call. I'll loop in Legal and Solutions. If hard-residency required, we must offer outage window SLA instead of cross-region fallback.

Sanjay: Adding a ticket to infra: "reservation quota per region" to prevent noisy tenant consuming all reserved capacity.

Claire: Great thread. If anyone sees missing items, drop them here. We'll capture into the spec doc and roadmap board after Fri sync. :rocket:
